intent: Render the platform's own select control in the kit's field chrome, so the browser owns the popup and the picking.
typical_uses: A form field whose choices are plain text, where the platform's own picker is an asset
A form field where the platform's own picker is wanted (native mobile picker, native typeahead)

dont_use_when.situation: Options carry more than plain text (an icon, a description, per-option styling)
A short list of choices that should all stay visible at once
An ordinary choice list with no reason to prefer the platform picker
A long list the user needs to search or filter

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

`className` merges onto the wrapper div around the <select> and `size` picks the wrapper's compact class - neither reaches the <select> itself; every other prop lands on the <select>, so an `aria-label` names the select (the element the platform exposes as the control, role combobox unless `multiple` makes it a listbox), never the wrapper.

`disabled` disables the <select> and stamps `data-disabled` on the wrapper, absent when enabled; native-select.module.css dims the whole wrapper, chevron included, with var(--opacity-disabled) off that attribute.

anti_patterns.dont: Restyle the picker's options with the kit's own theme tokens
anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave the option chrome to the platform - several engines (macOS, mobile) draw the native popup with OS colors whatever author CSS says, which is why the kit pins options and groups to the system Canvas colors instead of its own

a11y.by: native-select.test.tsx's "renders a native select with its options and the kit classes" assertion, which queries the control by its combobox role and its `aria-label` accessible name, and its "groups options under an optgroup label" assertion, which queries the group by role and name

unexposed_parts.reason: A <select> is a replaced element with no ::before or ::after, so the wrapper exists only to host the field chrome and position the chevron; it takes no role, and of the component's props only `className` and `size` style it (its `data-disabled` marker is derived from `disabled`, not a prop a consumer sets on it).
The dropdown indicator is rendered by the component itself, and no prop hides or replaces it - a select without its indicator reads as broken, so there is deliberately no slot for turning it off.

good.title: Uncontrolled select named for assistive tech
Grouped options under a label
good.code:
<NativeSelect aria-label="Timezone">
  <NativeSelectOptGroup label="Europe">
    <NativeSelectOption value="cet">Central European Time</NativeSelectOption>
  </NativeSelectOptGroup>
  <NativeSelectOption value="utc">Coordinated Universal Time</NativeSelectOption>
</NativeSelect>

bad.title: Rich option content
bad.why: The platform picker shows only the option's text, so the icon and the hint never appear. Rich item content is what Select is for.
